subject: Transportation Systems
title: The Battery Breakthrough
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Battery Breakthrough.

hook.text: In 2010, a kilowatt-hour of lithium-ion battery cost $1,100. By 2023, it was under $140.

buildup.text: Falling battery costs made electric vehicles competitive with combustion engines for the first time.

discovery.text: At around $100 per kWh, electric cars reach price parity with gasoline cars—no subsidies needed.

twist.text: Mining lithium and cobalt creates its own environmental damage. Batteries aren't perfectly green.

climax.text: Solid-state batteries promise 50% more range and faster charging. Several companies aim for 2027 production.

punchline.text: Cheaper batteries didn't just improve cars. They rewrote the future of transport.

quiz.question: At what battery cost per kWh do electric cars reach price parity with gasoline?
